title: Design System: Road to Next Rating

display.purpose: Verdicts, headlines, big claims. Stadium-signage authority; wordmark uses font-stretch 125%.

metric.purpose: The big number — readiness score, re-test deltas. Always tabular-nums.

body.purpose: The coach's speaking voice — explanations, buttons, descriptions.

label.purpose: Every eyebrow, unit, badge, and countdown. Always uppercase, always tracked wide — the instrument reading.

display-desktop.purpose: Top of the display voice — 80px on the marketing hero and the accent close.

h1-desktop.purpose: Desktop step of H1 — marketing section headings.

display-md.purpose: Mid step of the display voice — 64px.

marketing-h3.purpose: Step headings inside How It Works — deliberately close to the section heading so the screenshot stays the star.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one accent-colored action per screen (e.g. "Start the assessment").
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 52px; padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 14px; background: #D8E34C; color: #131408; font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, transform 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #E6EF7A; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D8E34C; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action alongside a primary CTA (e.g. "Continue with Google").
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { height: 52px; padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 14px; background: #1A1A1D; color: #F4F4F2; font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; border: 1px solid #2E2E33; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #4A4A50; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D8E34C; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Option Select Button
components.description: Signature assessment-question control. Selected state shows an accent border and a right-aligned accent dot.
components.css: .ds-option { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; min-height: 64px; width: 100%; padding: 14px 18px; border-radius: 16px; background: #131315; border: 1px solid #232327; color: #F4F4F2; font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.42; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease; } .ds-option:hover { border-color: #4A4A50; background: #17171A; } .ds-option--selected { background: rgba(216,227,76,0.08); border-color: #D8E34C; } .ds-option__dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; min-width: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #D8E34C; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Base content panel. An accent-tinted variant marks a callout worth noticing (e.g. the in-game-rule card).
components.html:

components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 20px; padding: 20px; background: #131315; border: 1px solid #232327; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-card--accent { border-color: #D8E34C; background: rgba(216,227,76,0.05); } .ds-card__eyebrow { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #80807B; } .ds-card__eyebrow--accent { color: #D8E34C; } .ds-card__title { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; color: #F4F4F2; margin: 0; } .ds-card__body { font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.6; color: #B0B0AB; margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field. Focus ring is the accent color (--ring binds to optic).
components.css: .ds-input { height: 48px; width: 100%; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 12px; background: #131315; border: 1px solid #2E2E33; color: #F4F4F2; font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #80807B; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D8E34C; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #D8E34C; }

components.name: Locked Card
components.description: The free-tier tease treatment: real content blurred behind a scrim, never a hard empty box. Used on Progress and Re-test Delta for free users.
components.html:
Readiness — 6 Weeks chart placeholder

Your readiness line, over time
components.css: .ds-locked { position: relative; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 20px; border: 1px solid #232327; background: #131315; padding: 20px; } .ds-locked__content { pointer-events: none; user-select: none; opacity: 0.45; filter: blur(7px); } .ds-locked__scrim { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 24px; text-align: center; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(19,19,21,0.4), rgba(19,19,21,0.7)); } .ds-locked__teaser { max-width: 240px; font-family: 'Instrument Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.4; color: #B0B0AB; margin: 0; }

components.name: Tab Bar
components.description: Text-only bottom navigation, deliberately iconless. Active indicator is a short accent tick above the label.
components.css: .ds-tabbar { display: flex; height: 64px; border-top: 1px solid #232327; background: #0B0B0C; } .ds-tabbar__item { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #80807B; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-tabbar__item:hover { background: #131315; } .ds-tabbar__item--active { color: #F4F4F2; } .ds-tabbar__tick { width: 16px; height: 2px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #D8E34C; } .ds-tabbar__item:not(.ds-tabbar__item--active) .ds-tabbar__tick { background: transparent; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small status chip. Color follows the shared state-color family so new states read as the instrument's reading changing, not new colors arriving.
components.html: On Track Due Today Plateau
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 5px 9px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.10em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-badge--optic { color: #D8E34C; background: rgba(216,227,76,0.12); } .ds-badge--warn { color: #E3B84C; background: rgba(227,184,76,0.12); } .ds-badge--danger { color: #E3654C; background: rgba(227,101,76,0.12); }

narrative.overview:
The whole interface is the logo happening at every scale. A flat, muted line — the rating a player has been stuck on — sits quietly under everything: near-black neutrals, mono labels, no shadows, no gradients, nothing raising its hand. Then, at the one moment that actually matters — the diagnosis, the accent CTA, the readiness number, the chart's rising line — a single optic yellow-green breaks upward off that flat line and takes the only color in the room. Calm and flat until the break; the break gets all the weight.

This is a deliberate rejection of two adjacent registers: the AI-dev-tool blue/navy gradient (reads as "software," not "coaching"), and the shouty fitness-app rainbow (reads as noise, not authority). Instead it borrows the workout-app register — stadium-signage type, tabular numbers, calibrated instrument labeling — because the product's whole claim is precision: not "here are ten drills," but "here is the one reading that matters." Mono labels in particular are what make the UI feel measured rather than decorated.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome-plus-one: every screen is near-black neutrals; optic yellow-green appears in exactly one place at a time.
Flat by construction: no shadows, no gradients; depth is tonal layering only.
Three voices, one job each: Archivo for verdicts, Instrument Sans for the coach's speaking voice, IBM Plex Mono for the instrument reading.
Nothing is centered except the reveal — the one screen where the whole UI stops and looks straight at the player.
The break (accent) is earned, not decorative: CTA, one data line, one selected state — never a background, never a heading.

rules.name: The Kill-the-Gradient Rule
rules.body: No gradients anywhere in the UI chrome. Gradients read as marketing; a blue-toward-green gradient specifically reads as "AI dev tool," which is the one register this product must not occupy.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Optic yellow-green never appears twice with two different meanings on the same screen, and never as a background fill behind body copy or a heading color. If nothing on a screen currently matters most, nothing is accented.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every metric and score uses tabular-nums so digits never shift width mid-count or mid-comparison.

rules.name: The Nothing-Italic Rule
rules.body: No italic anywhere in the system; emphasis comes from scale, weight, or the accent color, never from slant.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow is ever used. If a surface needs to read as "above" another, it gets a lighter neutral and/or a stronger border — never a shadow.

rules.name: The One Break Exception
rules.body: The marketing site's closing section is the single sanctioned inversion: the whole surface goes optic with optic-ink type on it. Scoped to that one section, on that one surface. It does not license accent fields anywhere else, and never inside the app.

dos: Do keep the accent to exactly one meaning per screen — one CTA, one data line, or one selected state, never more than one at a time.
Do use tabular-nums on every metric and score so digits align across a transition (old → new, countdowns).
Do uppercase and letter-space every mono label (0.10–0.22em depending on context) — this is what makes the UI read as calibrated rather than styled.
Do keep the locked/blur treatment honest: blur real content, keep the current headline number visible, never show a hard empty state on a paywalled card.
Do reserve reveal-bg (#060607) for the reveal and delta screens only — it signals "the app just went quiet to tell you something."
donts: Don't use a gradient anywhere in UI chrome — it reads as marketing, and specifically as "AI dev tool" in this palette.
Don't add a box-shadow to anything; depth comes from tonal layering and border weight only.
Don't italicize any text, or center any layout other than the reveal sequence.
Don't let the accent touch a background fill behind body copy or become a heading color — it marks a point, it never paints a surface.
Don't introduce a second accent hue for a new state; new states (warn, danger) must share the accent's lightness/chroma family so they read as "the same instrument, different reading."
